shared_elements: T-shaped pillar with broad head and narrower shaft carved in low relief
row of repeated quadrupeds in profile marching along the top register
horizontal dividing band with a row of short vertical strokes/hatching
profile animals in low relief on the shaft
elongated serpentine/curving animal on the lower shaft
small subsidiary animal figures filling the field between larger ones
justification: Both show the same distinctive scheme: a T-headed monolith whose upper head bears a row of profile quadrupeds above a horizontal band of short vertical strokes, with further low-relief profile animals (including a long-necked bird and elongated serpentine forms) stacked down the shaft, all rendered in the same flat, outlined, schematic-but-recognisable relief convention. The only differences are in the precise species and count of animals visible in each register, partly a consequence of the viewing angle and how much of the shaft is exposed.
